html:
The Chocholtecs, or Chocho, are an Indigenous people of the Mixteca Alta in northwest Oaxaca, Mexico, around Santa María Nativitas and Coixtlahuaca. Their language, Ngiigua, is one of the Popolocan languages of the Oto-Manguean family, close to Popoloca and Ixcatec.

In 1492 Coixtlahuaca was a rich town of mixed Chocholtec and Mixtec people, famous for its markets. The Aztec Triple Alliance conquered it in the 1450s and made it the head of a tribute province. A Dominican monastery was built there in the 1500s. Today only a few hundred people speak Chocholtec.
